title: Book One · Chapter 161: Two Small Numbers
story:
The first copied notice says the room opens at twelve. The real time is two. Ronan is eating lunch at school. He looks at the notice and sees the mistake.

He looks at the two marks. There is one extra line beside the two. It makes the number look like twelve. This notice was only a practice copy. But Leo used it to make three more. Those three will have the wrong time too.

“Stop,” Ronan says.

Leo looks up. “What?”

Ronan puts the old paper beside Miss Wu's original. Leo sees the difference. His face falls. He has worked all break to get the letters neat.

“We can change them,” Ronan says.

“They will look dirty.”

Mei puts a plain strip over the wrong number. The new time fits on it easily. She asks Miss Wu before they glue anything. They read the original with Miss Wu. “You can use the clean strips,” she says.

They check all four notices. Only practice papers have the wrong time. The adults have the invitations copied from Miss Wu's original. Those still say two until four. Ronan writes that on the list. They can leave the families' invitations as they are. No wrong invitations went home.

“We nearly opened during lunch,” Leo says.

“You could have shown people my rice,” Ronan tells him.

“A small bowl. An old spoon. Very true to life.”

They laugh and finish the correction. Each reads the new notices before the next person copies them. Mei reads the place. Leo reads the date. Ronan reads the hours. Then they read one whole notice together.

Miss Wu lets them put one on the classroom door. She keeps the others for the school entrance. She will choose places for those notices. Other school notices need space too.

On the way home Ronan checks the invitation in his own book. He knows it is right. He looks anyway, then stops. He has checked it and the time is right. He can put it away now.

At the green gate Mrs Lan asks, “Will there be food?” Ronan says no food is planned in the display room. She nods. “Then it will be easier to clear the room,” she says. His birthday cake was good. He nearly wanted cakes at the display too. Now he is glad he did not ask for them.

Mum comes out with a finished shirt. She asks him to hold a clean paper bag. Then she folds the shirt. He reads the customer's name on the bag. Then he puts the right shirt inside. He leaves the school papers in his bag. Mum is getting this shirt ready for its owner. Ronan helps her put it in the right bag.

After supper he tells Dad about the wrong hour. “Did any wrong invitations go out?” Dad asks. “We checked all four notices,” Ronan tells him. Dad nods and goes back to reading a work note.

Ronan feels pleased. He told the others about the wrong time. They checked all the papers and changed the wrong ones. Four practice notices have clean little strips on them. Real visitors still have the right time.

He puts his own notice on the shelf, away from the bell. Then he spends the rest of the evening reading the boat story. The boys in the story have made a bigger mistake. Can the boys fix their mistake? He wants to read on. He reads on and forgets the practice notices for a while.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：notice＝告示；original＝原件；correction＝更正。

情节提示：strip＝纸条；entrance＝入口；glue＝用胶水粘。

理解：1. 时间错误影响了哪些纸，没有影响哪些邀请？2. 三个孩子怎样核查更正后的内容？
